full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J: This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 29-7-2009 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal Nos. 63 of 2007 with First Appeal No.179 of 2007 allowing the appeals and, setting aside the judgment and decree dated 7-2-2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No.123 of 2006 decreeing the suit on contest without any order as to costs. 

 4. The trial Court upon hearing the parties by the judgment and order dated 7-2-2007 decreed the suit on contest against the defendant. 

 5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the defendant filed First Appeal No.63 of 2007 and the plaintiff filed First Appeal No.179 of 2007 before the High Court Division. 

 and decree dated 7-2-2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka, decreeing the suit on contest without any order as to costs. 

 “The Premises Rent Control Act, 1991 is a special law as far as the Rent Control is concern and it has been clearly stated in 17 DLR 306 that the specific provision of a special enactment must prevail over general enactments namely the general provisions of the Transfer of Property Act and it is further stated the landlord has been given this authority on the basis of section 20 of the Premises Rent Control Act,1991 and in view of the above, the judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division is illegal, malafide and,as such, liable to be set-aside. There is saving clause in section 20 of the Premises Rent Control Act,1991 in which it has been clearly stated that when a landlord accepts rent in respect of any premises sent by post money order by a tenant under section 18(5) or by the Controller under section 19(6) or withdraws any rent deposited under section 19, the fact of such acceptance or withdrawal shall not be used in any way as evidence that he has admitted as correct any of the particulars set forth in the postal money order form or in the application for deposit of such rent or that he has waived any notice to quit given by him to the tenant and withdrawal of rent from the office of the Rent Controller will not be treated as holding over under section 116 of Transfer of Property Act and the High Court Division did not consider this provision of law and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside.” 

 In the light of the findings, we find substance in this appeal. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned judgment delivered by the High Court Division is set-aside and the judgment and decree passed by the trail Court is hereby restored.
